iti100:2.2: The Buddha adapts a passage he elsewhere attributes to brahmins ([mn84:4.5]()). | “Bosom” is _orasa_, signifying a natural heir to a legitimately married couple (Manusmṛti 9.159, Skandapurāṇa 223.5, Kauṭilya’s Arthaśāstra 3.7). While _putta_ can mean “son” or “child”, in this case the gendered sense is required, since in Brahmanical context the concept is intended to explain how the male child takes precedence in inheritance (Manusmṛti 9.134). Thus the Buddha has both “bosom sons” ([thag21.1:71.4]()) and “bosom daughters” ([thig3.3:2.3](), [thig13.4:25.2]().
